items.title: Sakana AI launches standalone Namazu API, a Japanese-business-tuned fine-tune of Kimi K2.6
items.summary_en: Sakana AI moved its Namazu model from the consumer Sakana Chat product into a standalone, pay-as-you-go API. Namazu is described as an in-house fine-tune of Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K2.6, tuned on proprietary data for Japanese honorific speech (keigo) and business context, with an OpenAI-compatible interface and built-in web search and code execution tools. Sakana reported improvements over the Kimi K2.6 base on its JFBench Japanese-instruction benchmark and a large gain on a political-neutrality benchmark, and priced the API at roughly $0.95 per million input tokens and $4.00 per million output tokens; the service is not offered in the EU, UK, or Switzerland.
items.notes: Direct fetch of sakana.ai was blocked by the environment's network egress proxy this run; details corroborated across multiple independent secondary reports (BigGo Finance, AI Weekly, StartupHub.ai, Impress Watch) that cite the official sakana.ai/namazu-api/ page. Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and unverified by an independent evaluator.

items.title: Sakana AI retrains Fugu's 'conductor' orchestration model on a Gemma 4 base as a portability test
items.summary_en: Sakana AI published results of retraining the small 7B 'conductor' component of its Fugu orchestration system on a Google Gemma 4 base, having previously trained it on a Qwen base. The company described this explicitly as a portability/validation experiment rather than a production swap, and reported the Gemma-4-based conductor achieved orchestration performance comparable to the earlier version. Sakana framed the result as evidence that its lightweight conductor layer, which coordinates calls across a pool of larger frontier models, is not tied to a single underlying base model.
items.notes: Direct fetch of sakana.ai was blocked by the environment's network egress proxy this run; the official URL and date were confirmed via search-engine indexing and corroborated by a secondary analysis piece (Digital Applied) describing the same experiment. Sakana traces the underlying conductor and orchestration architecture to two of its own ICLR 2026 papers ('Trinity' and 'Conductor').

items.title: Sakana AI updates consumer Sakana Chat app with Fugu orchestrator, new Namazu generation, and code execution
items.summary_en: Sakana AI announced an update to its free consumer Sakana Chat service adding access to Sakana Fugu, its multi-model orchestration system, and an upgraded generation of the Sakana Namazu model, alongside new code-execution support that lets users preview model-generated code output directly inside the chat interface.
items.notes: Exact publication date is approximate (search snapshot showed the post as '15 hours old' at time of search on 2026-08-13, implying ~2026-08-12); direct fetch of sakana.ai was blocked by the environment's network egress proxy this run, so the post could not be read in full for exact timestamp or full feature list.

coverage_note: Three items found on Sakana AI's official blog (sakana.ai/blog) published within the roughly 10-day window ending 2026-08-13: the Namazu API launch (Aug 3), a Fugu conductor portability experiment on a Gemma 4 base (Aug 10), and a Sakana Chat product update bundling Fugu and a new Namazu generation (~Aug 12). Two earlier related releases (Fugu-Cyber, July 21; Fugu-Ultra v1.1 with Claude Code interface, July 24) fall outside the 10-day window and were excluded. Direct WebFetch access to sakana.ai was blocked by the environment's network egress proxy for this entire run, so all three items are marked 'primary-inferred' rather than 'primary-confirmed': official URLs and dates were verified via search-engine indexing, and content details were cross-checked against multiple independent secondary sources that cite and quote the same official pages.
